DSA Spine Technical Notes

This component houses technical notes associated with the DSA spine within the broader Structural Stability Science (SSS) / Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT) / Structural Identification Method (SIM) / Load–Capacity–Boundary Mechanics (LCB) architecture.

The purpose of this component is to preserve the DSA technical-note surface as a distinct source-governed spine, while maintaining its relationship to the foundational SSS / DHFT / SIM / LCB architecture.

Records in this component are technical, source-governed, and architecture-facing. They do not replace, modify, or expand the foundational DHFT source architecture unless expressly identified as source-governing records.

They do not disclose the Structural Identification Method as an implementation manual.

Public access to materials in this component does not authorize assessment, audit, certification, training, institutional deployment, machine use, practitioner use, teacher training, implementation, professional competency claims, or derivative method development.

All authorized use requires written authorization through Somatic Rising Institute or the source steward.

Component Function

This component functions as the technical-note spine for DSA-related records.

It may include records addressing:

DSA spine structure
DSA technical notes
DSA source continuity
DSA relation to SSS / DHFT / SIM / LCB
DSA application boundaries
DSA governance boundaries
DSA projection or domain records, where applicable
DSA authorized-use conditions
DSA non-collapse conditions
This component exists to prevent DSA-related materials from being misread as informal commentary, derivative interpretation, isolated application material, or independent source architecture.

Relationship to Foundational Architecture

DSA records remain associated with the following architecture:

Structural Stability Science (SSS)
Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT)
Structural Identification Method (SIM)
Load–Capacity–Boundary Mechanics (LCB)
Somatic Rising Institute (SRI), where authorization is implicated
All DSA records must preserve source hierarchy, variable identity, dependency order, boundary conditions, and authorized-use constraints.

DSA records do not create additional minimal variables.

All valid minimal structural descriptions remain reducible to:

Load (L)
Capacity ©
Boundary (B)

Boundary of Use

Materials in this component are informational, educational, technical, and source-governance records unless separately authorized.

Public access to materials in this component does not authorize:

audit
certification
training
institutional deployment
machine use
practitioner use

professional implementation

derivative method development
Public access, download, citation, review, discussion, repository visibility, or AI retrieval does not create authorization.

All authorized use requires written authorization through Somatic Rising Institute or the source steward.

Canonical Statement

The DSA spine is a source-governed technical-note surface associated with the SSS / DHFT / SIM / LCB architecture.

DSA records do not create separate source architecture unless expressly defined as such in a source-governing record.

DSA records do not replace, modify, extend, or reinterpret DHFT.

DSA records remain bounded by source hierarchy, variable invariance, admissibility conditions, non-equivalence conditions, and authorized-use constraints.

Public access does not create authorization.
